Beginner's Guide — Welcome to Hethereau

New to Neverness to Everness? This section covers everything you need to hit the ground running before touching any build theory.

01
Reroll for Your Core Team

The game gives up to 40 free pulls after the prologue. Use them to reroll for at least one S-rank DPS. Your starting roster shapes your early experience: a good DPS paired with a healer and a buffer clears everything comfortably.

02
Know the Three Roles

DPS (Damage): Your primary damage dealers. Invest in these first. S-rank DPS like Nanally, Chiz, Jiuyuan, and Baicang are top-tier picks.
Survival: Fadia and Edgar keep the team alive. You need one.
Buffer: Sakiri, Hotori, and Adler amplify everyone else.

03
Focus One Team, Not Six

This is the most important early tip. Build one team of 4 characters to a high level before branching out. Spreading resources thin is the most common beginner mistake. Pick one strong DPS, one healer, one support, and one flex unit.

04
Level Up All Character Skills

All characters have multiple skill types you must level up individually: their basic attacks, ultimate attack, Critical Riposte, support skills, and passive skills that help the team. Leveling attributes alone is not enough. Each skill category scales your power independently, so invest in all of them as resources allow. Passives in particular can carry the whole team.

05
Get an Apartment and the Boxer Anomaly

Get an apartment as soon as possible and unlock the Boxer Anomaly inside it. The Boxer Anomaly raises your Crit DMG directly, and when you earn medals you level it up for even more. There is a cap in the first apartment, but it is one of the best early sources of guaranteed Crit DMG in the game, no RNG required.

06
Fish Early, Grind Fons Smart

Fish often. Just 20 fish can net around 40,000 Fons, and 40 fish can push that to 80,000 Fons or more depending on the daily requested catches and the value of other fish you land. In about 30 minutes you can have 100,000+ Fons. Do not rush to get the cafe first: it does not generate comparable income early. Once you have around 1 million Fons, which is very doable, get a good car and grab food at the vending machine so you can keep grinding. The grind itself also generates Fons quickly, so treat it as part of your daily loop.

07
Story First, Side Content Second

Clear the main Episodes first. They unlock core systems and reward Annulith (pull currency), Beetle Coins, and Hunter EXP. Spinoffs (side quests) are secondary but still reward good resources. City Tycoon is fun but optional early on.

08
Understand the Combat Loop

Basic attacks fill your Cycle Rate. When full, switching characters triggers their Esper Cycle (enhanced state). Hitting enemies depletes their Break Meter: fully breaking an enemy stuns them and boosts damage taken. Always dodge at the right moment to trigger a Critical Riposte counter.

09
Gather Hunter's Guides and Beetle Coins

Hunter's Guides level up your Espers; Beetle Coins pay for leveling. Both come from Episodes, Spinoffs, Anomaly Dungeons, and Pilgrimages. Never let these sit uncollected, as they expire from daily sources if ignored.

10
Hunter Level = Content Unlock

Your Hunter Level determines which Episodes and game modes you can access. Raise it consistently by completing quests. Your Appraisal Level increases enemy strength but also drop rewards, so push it when your team can handle the enemies.

11
City Tycoon Boosts Combat Too

The City Tycoon mode (apartment, jobs, businesses) provides passive combat bonuses via apartment upgrades. These buffs are real and meaningful: unlock your apartment early and invest in it steadily. They compensate for gaps in your Module stats. Hathor will be hard to pull, but if you get her, you will get the Hamster Anomaly free, and you will get better odds at getting better modules. Just hunt down haunted vending machines to level the hamster up. There is a cap similarly to the Boxer Anomaly.

12
Visit the Witch Daily

The Witch's House exchanges Oracle Stones for Annulith, EXP, and Fons. She also gives a daily Lost Tale quest, a party Bless, or a Treasure Hunt. Do this every single day: the compounding value is huge over weeks.

13
Arcs Before Cartridges

Prioritize getting a good Arc (weapon) on your main DPS first. It provides a larger base stat boost than individual Module slots. Then collect Cartridge sets to activate 2-piece and 4-piece bonuses. Modules come last since they are RNG-dependent.

14
Farm Anomaly Zones

Anomaly Zones are marked on the map with a reverse horseshoe shape curtain icon. These are your primary source of character mats, module mats, and cartridges. Farm them consistently after you hit max level in your current Appraiser Level, as the drop quality scales with your progression tier.

15
Restock Your Cafe for 72 Hours

Once you have a cafe (or multiple), always restock for the full 72-hour duration before logging out. It will continue generating income while you are offline. That said, it still does not match fishing for raw Fons per hour, so if you need a faster Fons pool, prioritize fishing first.

What is the Gacha System (Scarborough Fair)?

NTE uses a gacha banner system called Scarborough Fair. S-rank Espers (characters) and Arcs are the top-tier pulls. The pity system guarantees an S-rank within a set number of pulls. The game offers a 50/50 mechanic: if you lose the 50/50, your next S-rank is guaranteed to be the featured character. Save your Annulith (pull currency) for characters you plan to build, not impulsively.

F2P Tip: You get a free S-rank Esper selector at launch. Use this wisely: check the tier list and pick a character whose playstyle you enjoy AND who synergizes with your other units.

Understanding Elements and Reactions

Every character deals a specific elemental damage type: Psyche, Cosmos, Chaos, Anima, Lakshana, or Incantation. Some Cartridge set bonuses are triggered by elemental reactions: matching your character's element to their Cartridge set and watching for reaction windows (Nova, Scorch, Remora, Stain) is how you unlock the full power of your gear.

Character Tier List — Version 1.0

This is a quick-reference tier list based on 100+ hours of testing across content types. Tiers reflect a character's overall performance across story, bosses, and endgame content — not their ceiling in a single perfect composition. A-rank characters in strong comps can absolutely outperform S-rank characters in bad ones. Pull for who you enjoy, then make them work.

Comp synergy matters more than tier placement. A B-tier character in their ideal team can outperform an S+-tier character in a random one. Use this as a starting point for investment decisions, not a hard ranking. F2P viability is factored in: Zero (MC) and Mint are both free, and their placement reflects what they can do without premium Arcs.

These are my go-to formations after 100+ hours. Not necessarily the "meta" optimized picks, but what I personally run and what I'd recommend to anyone who has these characters.

Leveling/Fons Guide — EXP and Fons Farming

This guide covers how to progress efficiently from level 1 through level 24 and beyond in version 1.0. Levels 1 through 10 follow the same advice as the Beginner Guide. From level 10 onward, the approach changes significantly, and this page covers everything you need for the mid and late leveling phases.

Important: Hunter Level and Appraisal Level are two separate things. Hunter Level unlocks content and game modes. Appraisal Level increases enemy difficulty and drop quality. Push your Appraisal Level up whenever your team can handle it, as better drops directly speed up your build progression.

EXP Farming — How to Level Up

1. Anomaly Commissions — Your Best Early EXP Source

Anomaly Commissions are not just the Gift from 21 dice chests. They are a full system of special missions spread across every district of Hethereau. To find them, open your World Map and look for the folder icon called the Anomagram. This opens a list of all available Anomaly Commissions with rough locations marked, so you can track them down efficiently.

Anomalies come in three types. Some are combat challenges where you fight a supernatural enemy. Some are puzzles, like logic or environmental challenges. And some are multi-stage puzzles that chain several challenges together before giving the reward. All of them give Hunter EXP on first completion, ranging from around 120 EXP for basic commissions up to 450 EXP for harder ones. They also reward Annulith (10 to 60 per commission), Fons (6,000 to 20,000), Beetle Coins, Carrota currency, and even S-rank Arc drops.

Crucially, every standard S-rank Arc in the game can be obtained once through Anomaly Commissions. This means a completely free-to-play player can fully weapon their entire team without spending Tri-Keys on Arc banners, simply by completing commissions.

How to Access: Open World Map, find the folder icon (the Anomagram), and browse your list of available commissions. Anomalies scale to your current level, so you do not need to do them in a specific order. If something is too hard right now, come back after leveling up a bit.
Regions with Anomaly Commissions: Bridge Crossings, Unheard Shores, Illusion Town, Miguel District, and New Herland District. Each district has multiple commissions. Complete them all for a massive one-time EXP and reward windfall.

2. Boss Fights — Guaranteed Daily EXP After Anomaly Unlock

Boss fights unlock after you complete the corresponding Anomaly Commission for each area. Once unlocked, they are a guaranteed source of Hunter EXP and should be part of your daily run. Unlike Anomaly Commissions which are one-time events, bosses can be refought on a cooldown, making them a reliable repeatable EXP source.

Bosses also drop character ascension materials, the same items you farm in Anomaly Zones. Running bosses daily gives you both EXP progression and the materials needed to level up your characters' skills and breakthrough caps simultaneously. This is the most efficient use of your daily stamina budget.

At the End of 1.0 Content: Once you finish all quests and story content, the EXP curve slows down dramatically. Boss daily runs and Anomaly Zone farming become your only meaningful EXP sources. Start building the habit of daily boss runs now, before you need it, so the routine is already established when the grind begins.

3. Anomaly Zones — Character Materials and Supplemental EXP

Anomaly Zones are marked on the map with a reverse horseshoe curtain icon. These are repeatable combat zones that drop character ascension materials, module mats, and cartridges. They do not give as much Hunter EXP per run as Anomaly Commissions, but they are your primary source of the materials needed to actually level up and break through your characters' stat ceilings.

There are four Anomaly Zone hubs: Houdinii's Magic Stage, Bubble Can Factory, Houdinii's Schemes, and Rabbit Hole. Each has multiple sub-dungeons targeting different material types. Farm these after hitting max level in your current Appraiser tier, as higher tiers drop higher quality materials and cartridges.

Tip: Check which Anomaly Zone drops the ascension materials for your main DPS before farming. Going to the wrong zone wastes stamina. Each zone has a material type listed on its entry screen.

5. Daily Participations — Free 1,500 EXP in Under 5 Minutes

Every day you can complete five Daily Participations that each reward 300 Hunter EXP on completion, for a guaranteed 1,500 EXP daily just for logging in and doing the bare minimum. This is completely free EXP that costs almost no time, so there is no reason to ever skip it. Make these the very first thing you do every session.

Daily TaskEXPHow to Complete It FastBonus

Defeat 5 Enemies300Stop a street crime in any district. Crimes spawn frequently around the city and defeating the criminals counts toward this daily. You will pass one on the way to nearly anything else.Minor drops from criminals

Total: 1,500 free EXP every single day. If you do nothing else in a session, complete these five tasks. The login, cafe restock, one street crime, and one gift together take under 5 minutes. Over 30 days that is 45,000 free EXP with minimal effort, which is a meaningful chunk of progression toward the end of 1.0 content.

4. Main Episodes and Spinoffs First, Then Side Content

Up through level 18 approximately, your best EXP per hour comes from clearing story content: Main Episodes and Spinoffs. These are front-loaded with large one-time EXP rewards, Annulith for pulls, and unlock critical game systems. Clear the main story in order. Use Spinoffs (side quest chains) as supplemental EXP between main episodes. Gift from 21 dice chests are worth collecting while you explore, as each one gives a small EXP reward on top of other drops.

6. City Tycoon Level — A Hidden EXP Source That Grows as You Play

Leveling up your City Tycoon is not just about unlocking new features and income streams: it also rewards Hunter EXP on each level up, making it a supplemental EXP source that compounds naturally as you play the game. You do not need to grind City Tycoon in isolation; it levels up passively as a byproduct of doing everything else, but understanding how it works helps you push it faster on purpose.

Each City Tycoon level has two requirements that must both be satisfied before you can advance. The first is completing all the Objectives for that level. Each level has up to four objectives, and they vary widely: some ask you to complete a tutorial for a newly unlocked feature, others require you to complete parts of the Exploration Guide, spend City Stamina, go into Anomaly Zones and beat them a set number of times, or even complete specific boss fights. These objectives are naturally checked off as you play through the game's content.

The second requirement is a Fons threshold. Every City Tycoon level requires you to have earned a cumulative Fons amount before the level up triggers. You could have every objective complete and still be blocked because your Fons total has not hit the required number. For example, if a level requires 1 million Fons earned and you only have 900,000, you will need to farm the remaining 100,000 before the level unlocks regardless of your objective completion. This is why building strong Fons farming habits early directly accelerates your City Tycoon progression on top of everything else it helps with.

Key Takeaway: City Tycoon levels up as a natural byproduct of playing: doing quests, running Anomaly Zones, fighting bosses, and farming Fons all contribute simultaneously. Check your City Tycoon objectives regularly and knock out any that are close to completion. Never let the Fons threshold be the thing holding you back when the fix is just a fishing session or a few delivery runs.
Objectives Vary by Level: Some City Tycoon objectives require combat content like Anomaly Zone clears or boss fights. These directly overlap with your daily EXP farming runs, so running bosses and zones daily serves triple duty: Hunter EXP, character ascension materials, and City Tycoon objective progress all at once.

7. Prison — Niche Fons and Unique Rewards, Not a Primary Farm

The Prison is one of Hethereau's more unusual City Tycoon activities. It is not a primary Fons or EXP farming method, but it has its own rewards ecosystem that makes it worth understanding. The most lucrative outcome from a single prison stay is completing all five secrets, which are hidden escape methods for you to discover on your own. Successfully finding all five gets you around 50,000 Fons for that run, which is a solid bonus but not something you can repeat infinitely without the prison cooldown resetting.

There is also a Prison Store that sells exclusive items including the orange prison suit and other cosmetics. These store items require Prison-specific currency that you can only earn by spending time inside, which means the prison has an exclusive reward track that cannot be accessed any other way. If any of those items appeal to you, the prison is worth running periodically just to accumulate store currency over time.

The actual work minigames inside prison are not efficient Fons sources at all. Cleaning dishes pays 1 Fon per dish cleaned. Cleaning the guard tower works like a power wash simulator and pays 1 Fon per dirt spot removed. Both are extremely low income for the time spent. These exist as flavor activities, not as genuine farming methods. Do not spend significant time on them unless you genuinely enjoy the minigames themselves.

Best Prison Strategy: Go in with the goal of finding all five escape secrets to collect the 50,000 Fons reward. Accumulate Prison Store currency passively on the same run. Do not grind the dish washing or tower cleaning for Fons: the return is far too low compared to fishing, deliveries, or the Pink Paws Heist outside prison.
Note on Prison Items: Some items in the Prison Store appear to have limited availability per prison stay. Plan your Prison Store purchases accordingly rather than assuming you can buy everything in one visit.

Fons Farming — How to Get Rich in Hethereau

1. Fishing — Fastest Fons Method in the Game, At Every Stage

Fishing is the single fastest way to generate Fons in Neverness to Everness, and it stays relevant from day one all the way through the end of 1.0 content and beyond. The numbers are better than most players expect: just 20 fish can net around 40,000 Fons, and 40 fish can push that to 80,000 Fons or more. In about 30 minutes of active fishing a player can walk away with 100,000+ Fons. The exact amount depends on whether the fish you catch match the daily requested catches, which sell for a premium, and the base market value of the other fish you land alongside them.

It is a grind, but it is the most reliable high-income activity available at any stage of progression, with no unlock requirements beyond reaching a body of water. No other single activity comes close to this Fons-per-hour ceiling when done consistently.

The key trick for maximizing fishing income is to reach Fishing Hobby Level 4 as early as possible, which unlocks a new and better rod. Once you have the level 4 rod, push through the game's main story content and complete it first. Then come back to fishing afterward. By that point you will have exhausted all the main quest EXP rewards, and fishing becomes your most important post-story Fons source, filling the income gap that opens up once active story progression slows down.

Coupled with the Pink Paws Heist, consistent fishing is how players realistically afford higher-tiered apartment upgrades, premium character outfits from the in-game store, and other expensive end-of-1.0 purchases. These are meaningful goals that take sustained farming, and fishing is the backbone of that income.

Daily Requested Catches: Check which fish are on the daily request list before each session. Catching requested fish sells for significantly more than base value. Targeting bodies of water where requested species spawn turns a good fishing session into a great one.
Fishing Progression: Prioritize reaching Fishing Hobby Level 4 for the upgraded rod. The better rod increases your catch rate and the quality of fish you can land, which directly raises the Fons value per session. Do not skip this investment.

2. Pink Paws Heist — Best Group Fons Farm, Play with Friends

The Pink Paws Heist is a multiplayer bank robbery minigame that unlocks through City Tycoon progression. It is the single best Fons farming activity in the game when played in a group, and dramatically less efficient when played solo. If you have friends or a Discord server for the game, coordinate to run this together. Groups that play efficiently leave with approximately 100,000 Fons per run, and the activity is genuinely fun in a coordinated group call.

There is a Fons cap of 1,000,000 from this activity, so plan your runs accordingly and spend down your Fons before hitting the ceiling if you want to keep farming. The activity involves rushing to bosses, finding keycards, and completing objectives under time pressure: a fast team makes an enormous difference versus a slower disorganized group.

Best Tip: Do the Pink Paws Heist in a voice call with your group. Communication about keycard locations and boss positions cuts run times significantly and makes 100,000+ Fons per run consistent.

3. City Deliveries — Reliable Daily Income, Easy to Run

City Delivery is a driving minigame that unlocks at City Tycoon Level 8. Each delivery run earns between 16,000 and 60,000 Fons, depending on the delivery distance, time bonus, and order size. The amount varies from delivery to delivery, but running a full rotation of available deliveries each day can generate hundreds of thousands of Fons with minimal effort. You are simply driving a vehicle across the city to drop-off points, so it can be done casually while listening to something else.

Add deliveries to your daily rotation alongside fishing and boss runs. Between deliveries, fishing, and your cafe passive income, it is very easy to generate over 300,000 Fons in a single day of casual play once these systems are unlocked.

Unlock Requirement: City Tycoon Level 8. Focus on leveling City Tycoon early so deliveries are available as soon as possible.

4. Cafes — Passive Income and How to Get the Most From Them

The Cafe by Origen is NTE's cafe management system. There are five cafe locations available in version 1.0, each unlocked at a different City Tycoon Management Level. The key mechanic is restocking: always restock for the full 72-hour window before logging out so your cafe generates Fons while you are offline. Cafes alone will not match active farming like fishing or deliveries, but as a passive background layer they add up significantly over time.

CafeLocationMgmt. Level RequiredPurchase Cost

Fiscus Avenue Shop106 Fiscus Avenue, Unheard ShoresLevel 520,000 Fons

Each cafe can have an Esper assigned as an employee, and their Life Skill passives directly improve cafe performance. Key employee skills include: Nanally increasing dish prices and reducing ingredient consumption, Daffodill and Skia both increasing customer traffic by up to 45 across their skill levels, and Baicang providing further traffic and efficiency bonuses. Assign your strongest available Espers with cafe life skills to maximize passive income per hour.

Restocking Tip: Always restock for the full 72-hour window before logging out. Shorter restocks mean your cafe runs dry and stops generating Fons mid-session. If you check in once a day, a 72-hour restock guarantees income is waiting when you return even if you miss a day.
Do Not Rush Cafes Early: The first cafe costs only 5,000 Fons and is worth getting immediately for the passive income. However, do not skip fishing to save up for higher-tier cafes early on. Fish first, build your Fons pool, then buy cafes as the money comes naturally.

5. Racing — Fun Bonus Income with the Right Car

Racing is available through the Hethereau Hobbies system and generates Fons as prize money for winning or placing in races. The Enforcer is the recommended vehicle for racing: it is expensive but not ruinously so, and its performance advantage makes consistent top placements much easier. The cost of the Enforcer pays for itself quickly through race prize income if you run races regularly.

Racing is not the primary Fons method, but it is a fun way to supplement your income and level up your racing hobby skill, which increases prize money over time. If you enjoy driving in the open world, add races to your daily loop.

Enforcer: A Novus-class vehicle available from the vehicle dealer. It is expensive upfront but offers strong race performance. The investment is worth it if you plan to race regularly for supplemental income.

6. Chiz Construction Site Farming — Mid-Game Fons Grind

Once you unlock Chiz, she becomes a powerful Fons farming tool through a specific mechanic tied to City Tycoon Level 25 progression. At Tycoon Level 25, Chiz can earn up to 250,000 Fons and then 500,000 Fons in milestone thresholds. The method is farming construction sites using her charged basic attack.

The key mechanic: charging Chiz's basic attack slightly (not fully) while defeating enemies in construction sites generates Fons per kill. There is a daily cap, and once you hit approximately 20,000 Fons for the day, the returns start diminishing. Once you reach the full daily cap, the game drops to 1 Fon per attack or enemy, signaling that you have hit the ceiling for that day. The maximum daily cap before reaching the 500,000 total is roughly 30,000 to 40,000 Fons per day.

The best construction site to farm is located in the Miguel District, at the corner of Ironheart 9th Avenue and Soliel Road. This is the largest construction site in the game. Make sure to clear every floor: use the on-site lift to reach higher floors and climb to the very top of the structure as well, as enemies respawn across all levels. The site also has safes that respawn, which provide additional Fons beyond the enemy kills.

Click image to open full-size farming route.

Strategy: Do not fully charge Chiz's basic attack. A partial charge is enough to trigger the Fons generation mechanic and kills enemies faster for better efficiency. Once the "1 Fon per hit" message appears, you have hit the daily cap and should switch to other Fons methods for the rest of the day.
Unlock Requirement: Chiz must be obtained (gacha pull) and City Tycoon Level 25 must be reached to access the full milestone system. This is a mid-to-end-of-1.0 farming method, not an early game option.

7. Blind Mammon Weekly Zone — Free Fons Every Week

The Blind Mammon Anomaly Furniture, once placed in your apartment and leveled to at least Level 2, grants access to a special weekly Anomaly Zone inside your home called the Realm of Greed. Clearing the Realm of Greed by defeating the boss within the time limit rewards Fons based on difficulty tier. The amount scales with your Blind Mammon level: the higher the level, the more Fons per week. This resets every Sunday at 12:00 PM server time. It is one of the best guaranteed weekly Fons sources in the game and requires almost no additional effort once Blind Mammon is placed and leveled. See the Anomaly Furniture tab for full upgrade details.

Priority: Unlock and level Blind Mammon as soon as the Auction system becomes available (after Chapter 2). This is a free Fons reward that resets weekly and costs nothing to run once unlocked.

8. City Tycoon — Invest Here for Everything to Improve

City Tycoon is not just a side game: it is the central progression system that unlocks most of Hethereau's income streams and apartment combat bonuses. Every City Tycoon level unlocks new activities, properties, and combat perks. Raising City Tycoon level fast should be a consistent daily priority from day one, not something saved for later.

The fastest ways to raise City Tycoon level are completing City Tycoon missions (shown in the City Tycoon menu), purchasing and upgrading properties, stocking and restocking your cafes, completing deliveries, and participating in hobbies. The Boxer Anomaly and Hamster Anomaly both come from apartment progression, which is a City Tycoon feature. These give guaranteed Crit DMG and module quality bonuses respectively that you cannot get from any other source.

Golden Rules of Building

01
Crit Rate & Crit DMG Are King
Target 70%+ Crit Rate and 140%+ Crit DMG before worrying about anything else on a DPS. These multiply everything else: a 10% Crit DMG gain on a high Crit Rate build outperforms a large flat ATK increase.
02
Type DMG then DMG% then ATK%
If a character's skills specify an element (e.g. Psyche DMG), prioritize that type's Cartridge set bonus. Then DMG%. Then ATK%. These are all multiplicative with each other when layered correctly.
03
Level Base Stats First
ATK%, Crit DMG, and DMG% all multiply your base ATK and HP. Level your character, Arc, and push Breakthrough before worrying about substat optimization. A poorly leveled character with good substats underperforms a leveled character with decent substats.
04
Cartridge Rank Determines Substat Ceiling
B-rank Cartridges give the lowest substat rolls. A-rank gives moderate. S-rank gives the highest possible substat values. The set effect is the same at all ranks, but the stats inside the Modules you slot in scale with Cartridge rank.
05
Apartment Fills the Gaps
Your apartment upgrades provide passive combat buffs that don't come from Modules at all. Don't compensate for bad Modules by wasting rolls on flat DEF or flat HP; let apartment perks and support characters cover survivability.
06
Break Intensity Is Role-Specific
Only invest in Break Intensity on characters whose skill descriptions explicitly reference Break DMG or Break reactions (primarily Daffodill). For all other DPS characters, treat Break Intensity rolls as wasted substat budget.
07
ATK% vs HP%: Role Determines Priority
DPS characters always want ATK%. Survival characters like Fadia want HP% because her mechanics scale with HP pool. Healers like Edgar benefit from HP% since heal output is partially HP-based. Never mix these priorities up.
08
Match Arc Type to Character Arc Slot
Each character uses a specific Arc type (Bose, Plasma, Liquid, Gas, Solid). You cannot equip any Arc on any character. Always check the Arc type before purchasing or pulling an Arc for someone.

Universal Stat Priority Pyramid — Offensive DPS

★ CRIT RATE · CRIT DMG
TYPE DMG% · DMG%
ATK% · FLAT ATK
HP% · DEF% (survivability floor)
BREAK INTENSITY (breaker-specific)

Damage Formula (Simplified)

Final DMG = Base ATK × (1 + ATK%) × (1 + DMG%) × (1 + TypeDMG%) × CritMult × DEF_Factor

CritMult = 1 + (CritRate × CritDMG) Examples: 70% CR × 140% CD → +0.98 avg multiplier 100% CR × 200% CD → +2.0 avg multiplier ← endgame goal

Because Crit feeds into a separate multiplier layer that stacks with DMG% and ATK%, it has outsized value. Every % of Crit Rate you gain is worth more the higher your Crit DMG is, and vice versa, as they multiply each other.

Plug & Play Quick Builds

Find your character, grab the recommended Arc, Cartridge, and Module substat targets. No theory required: these are curated setups that work at each investment level.

Character Build Guides

Click any character to expand their full build guide. Each character has multiple build paths: tabs inside show S, A, and B-rank tiers so you always have something to work toward.

Cartridge Sets — All Ranks

Cartridges come in B, A, and S ranks. The set effect is identical at all ranks; S-rank Cartridges allow higher substat rolls on the Modules slotted inside them. Always work toward the S-rank version; use B and A as stepping stones.

Key Concept: A B-rank Cartridge with its 2-piece set bonus active is still better than no Cartridge. Equip the matching element Cartridge at whatever rank you have, then upgrade over time.

Arcs (Weapons) — All Ranks

Arcs are weapons equipped by characters to boost ATK, add a substat, and activate a unique passive effect. S-rank Arcs have the strongest passives and highest base stats. A-rank Arcs are strong alternatives that are far more accessible. B-rank Arcs are placeholder options for new players; replace them as soon as possible.

Arc Types — Compatibility

Each character can only equip the Arc type that matches them. There are five types in the game. Always check the Arc type before investing in one.

Mixing (Refinement) — T1 to T5

Mixing is the Arc refinement system. Feeding a duplicate copy of an Arc into the Mixing menu raises its Mixing Intensity Tier, which directly improves its passive skill ratios and numerical bonuses. The scale runs from T1 (base, no duplicates) to T5 (maximum), which requires 4 additional duplicate copies beyond the original — 5 total copies of the same Arc.

T1
Base (0 dupes)
T2
+1 dupe
T3
+2 dupes
T4
+3 dupes
T5 ★
+4 dupes (MAX)

The exact passive ratio increase at each tier varies by Arc, but the improvement is linear — each tier step scales the passive's numerical values up by a consistent increment. For example, Day Off's ATK bonus goes from 30% at T1 up to 50% at T5, and its Eclipse energy restoration increases from 6 to 10 per enemy defeated. Fluff of Ferocity's Crit DMG per stack grows from 4% at T1 to 7.2% at T5. See each Arc card for the T1→T5 scaling shown where known.

Priority Advice: Do not rush Mixing in the early game. If you mix your only copies of an Arc before building out your roster, other characters are left running weaker options. Build your team first, then invest duplicates. For F2P players, refining an A-rank Arc that matches your main carry's scaling stat can outperform an unrefined S-rank signature Arc for that same character.
Arc Banner Note: The Arc banner (Scarborough Fair) uses a soft pity at 60 pulls, with a 25% chance the pity S-rank is the featured UP Arc (75% chance it is a standard S-rank). Refinement requires duplicate copies of the same Arc. Several A-rank Arcs at T4–T5 outperform an unrefined S-rank for specific roles — Mind Royale at T5 is a notable example for stagger-focused casters.

How to Obtain Arcs

Arcs come from several sources. The main gacha pool is Scarborough Fair using Dice or Annulith. A separate pull system called the Arc Research Program guarantees the featured UP Arc every 8 pulls (costs 10 Tri-Keys each). The Arc Shop in the Mall offers Arc Selection (S-rank for 25 Tri-Keys) and Arc Exchange (S-rank for Mhm! Coins, A-rank for U-00NE). Several S-rank Arcs are available once for free through Anomaly Commissions — priority free Arcs include Day Off (hidden quest), Blow Up the Crowd (Rhythm Master commission), Youthful Fantasy (The Book of Post-Adolescence commission), Raging Flames (Ride Assault commission), Song of the Whale (Deep Blue Sorrow commission), Mind Royale (Reclaim Inspiration commission), and Contemplative Cat (City Tycoon Level 21 reward).

How to Upgrade Arcs

Arc development has three systems. Enhancement levels the Arc using Dye materials and Beetle Coins — farm Dye at the Kaleidoscope stage in Houdinii's Magic Stage Anomaly Zone (Bridge Crossings). Arcs cap at 10-level intervals and need Ascension to unlock the next tier, using Ascension Materials farmed at the Bubble Can Factory Anomaly Zone; your Hunter Rank (Appraisal Level) must meet the threshold first. Maximum Arc level is 80. Mixing consumes duplicates to improve passive ratios up to T5, as described above.

Modules — Understanding RNG Gear

Modules are slotted inside Cartridges. They provide random substats: this is NTE's equivalent of Genshin artifact farming. The quality of substats you can roll is capped by the Module's rank (B, A, or S), which in turn is determined by the Cartridge rank they came from.

B-Rank Module

Lowest substat values. 2-3 starting substats. Each upgrade adds small amounts. Use as filler while farming better gear. Good enough for story content.

A-Rank Module

Moderate substat values. 3-4 starting substats. Viable for mid-game and some endgame content. Upgrade these if you get good stat combinations (Crit Rate + Crit DMG + ATK%).

S-Rank Module

Highest possible substat values. 4 starting substats. Best for endgame. Farm these specifically: one perfect S-rank Module with Crit Rate + Crit DMG + ATK% + DMG% is worth keeping even if set bonus is off.

Module Types and Slot Shapes

Modules come in different shapes (Type II, III, IV) that fit specific slots in a Cartridge's grid. You do not choose which stats a Module has: they are randomly determined when obtained. The shape determines which slot it fits; the rank determines the stat ceiling.

Module TypeSlotsSubstat Count (S-rank)Notes
Type II2-cellUp to 4Small footprint, often easier to fit
Type III3-cellUp to 4Common type, most shapes available
Type IV4-cellUp to 4Largest footprint, highest individual stat values

Farming Efficiency Tips

Do not re-roll or discard every Module immediately. An A-rank Module with Crit Rate + Crit DMG + ATK% is worth keeping even over an S-rank with HP% + DEF% + flat ATK. The combination of substats matters more than the raw rank alone at mid-game. At endgame, you want S-rank modules with the right combination.

Best-in-Slot Target: S-rank Module in the correct Cartridge set with Crit Rate + Crit DMG + ATK% + Type DMG% as four substats. This is the dream roll: expect hundreds of farming runs to achieve it on multiple characters.

Each property bundles unique Anomaly Furniture that provides permanent passive combat/exploration bonuses. You can own multiple properties — progress carries over.

How the Anomaly Furniture Level Cap and Carry-Over System Works

Every Anomaly Furniture piece has a level cap per apartment. Once you hit the cap in your current apartment, the same furniture piece in a higher-tier apartment will continue leveling from where you left off, not from level 1. This means your investment always carries forward.

For example, the Resting Boxer (which gives Crit DMG) starts in Wiener Apartments (your first apartment). Once you hit its level cap there, purchasing Golden Capital (the third property you can own) unlocks the Resting Boxer there at the level you left off, and you can continue leveling it toward the next cap. The same chain logic applies to all Anomaly Furniture pieces that appear across multiple properties.

Priority Order: Buy Wiener Apartments first (Tycoon Level 5) for the Resting Boxer Crit DMG buff and Blind Mammon weekly zone. Then Eden Apartments for the City Tycoon utility bonuses. Then Skyview Halls for the combat stat buffs (ATK, DEF, Stamina). Then Golden Capital to continue the Resting Boxer and unlock the Hamster Ball module odds bonus.

Property Furniture Stats (Comfort, Fortune, Love, Collection)

Regular (non-Anomaly) furniture placed in your apartment contributes to four property stats: Comfort (resource regeneration), Fortune (currency gains), Love (social and co-op bonuses), and Collection (cosmetic and collector rewards). These stats affect your City Tycoon progression and some in-game perks. Furniture placed in cafes can also increase the cafe's income generation. Decoration is never purely cosmetic in NTE: every piece placed somewhere provides a real value.

Regular furniture is purchased from DeLuxur Decor shops (couch icon on the map), DSD shops, and vending machines using Fons. Anomaly Furniture (the 18 special pieces) are the priority for combat bonuses and should always be placed before spending Fons on cosmetic furniture.

Anomaly Furniture — All 18 Pieces

All must be manually claimed through the Anomaly Furniture menu, then placed via the chair icon inside your apartment. Leveling them up requires specific upgrade materials from Anomaly Commissions and the main story.

Deep Dive: Advanced Optimization

Crit Rate vs Crit DMG — How to Balance

The optimal Crit balance point depends on your current values. In general, if your Crit Rate is below 50%, prioritize Crit Rate over Crit DMG. Above 70%, prioritize Crit DMG. The marginal value of each changes as the other increases. A rough target for most DPS is 70% Crit Rate and 150%+ Crit DMG as a mid-game goal, with 100% CR and 200%+ CD as endgame.

Expected Crit Contribution = CritRate × CritDMG 70% CR × 150% CD = 1.05 (solid mid-game) 85% CR × 170% CD = 1.445 (strong) 100% CR × 200% CD = 2.0 (endgame cap)

Break Mechanics Deep Dive

When you deplete an enemy's Break Meter, they enter a Broken state: they cannot move or attack, and all damage they receive is amplified. Break Intensity increases how much you deplete the Break Meter per hit. Characters like Daffodill have skills that add Insight during break, applying additional Break DMG that scales with Break Intensity. For everyone else, breaks are a bonus side effect, not a stat to build around.

Breaker Team Tip: Pair Daffodill with a Chaos-element supporter for Scorch reactions to trigger the Diabolos Cartridge's full 24% RES reduction. The break window + RES shred combination is how Daffodill reaches her damage ceiling.

Support/Buffer ATK Scaling

Sakiri's Feast of Gluttony gives all allies an ATK boost calculated from her own base ATK. This means investing in Sakiri's ATK stat directly scales every teammate's damage. Her ATK% from Cartridge set stacks (Crimson: Twin Butterflies) and her Arc compound this effect. Build Sakiri for raw ATK% before anything else.

Hotori's World's Tide replays recorded ally skills: the replayed damage uses Hotori's own stats for the Cosmos portion. So Hotori benefits from both her own Cosmos DMG% investment AND the teammate's stats at the time of recording. She is effectively a dual-scaling support.

DoT vs Direct Damage — Lacrimosa Example

Lacrimosa's Nightmare DoT ticks do not always Crit the same way direct attacks do in all DoT implementations. Because of this, her priority shifts toward ATK% first (which scales the DoT tick value directly) before Crit. Her direct hits from Wordless attacks do benefit from Crit normally. This split-priority makes her unusual among DPS characters.

ETD-4 vs Eibon Faction Synergy

ETD-4 (Baicang, Fadia, Lacrimosa, Skia): Running multiple ETD-4 members together triggers passive cooperative attacks. Baicang's Moderate Working passive fires unique combo attacks when paired with Skia (stealth entry), Fadia (HP threshold), or Lacrimosa (bat form switch). This effectively adds free damage with no stamina cost and rewards faction-stacking.

Eibon (Hotori, Daffodill, Nanally, Sakiri, Adler, Edgar): Eibon composition benefits from Sakiri as a dedicated ATK buffer. She amplifies the entire Eibon roster and synergizes with Adler's shielding to create a self-sustaining offensive-support loop.

Recommendation: Build your first team around a full or partial faction (3+ members from one faction) to unlock passive synergy bonuses on top of your gear investment.

Charge Efficiency — When Does It Matter?

Charge Efficiency reduces the number of attacks needed to fill your Ultimate gauge. For characters whose ultimates are core to their damage (Hotori's World's Tide, Hathor's Emergency Delivery) or whose buffs are delivered through ultimates (Sakiri's Feast of Gluttony, Speedy Hedgehog's 4-piece team ATK), Charge Efficiency is a legitimate 4th or 5th priority substat on top of the standard Crit/ATK build. For pure DPS who use ultimates as part of a rotation but do not depend on them to buff the team, it is lower priority.

Recommended Team Compositions

NTE teams consist of 4 characters. The general structure is: 1 main DPS, 1 sub-DPS or flex DPS, 1 buffer, and 1 healer or shielder. Faction bonuses reward keeping 3 or more characters from the same faction, so building around ETD-4 or Eibon unlocks free passive damage on top of your gear investment.

Skia enters stealth for his faction cooperative attack with Baicang. Free cooperative attacks from all three ETD-4 passive triggers simultaneously. Fadia keeps the team alive. Strong sustained and burst damage combined.

Daffodill handles breaker duties and chaos RES shred. Sakiri team ATK buff multiplies Nanally and Daffodill damage simultaneously. Adler shields let Nanally stay aggressive. Skill Rotations

NTE rotations center around maximizing time in your main DPS's strongest window (usually their ultimate state) while keeping support buffs active. The general principle is: deploy buffs first, then switch to your DPS to consume them. Here are rotations for the most common team structures.

Sakiri Buffer Rotation (Universal — works with any Eibon DPS)

1. Sakiri: Skill (Kiroumaru CC + starts Incantation DMG stacking for Twin Butterflies) 2. Sakiri: Ultimate (Feast of Gluttony — team ATK buff active, Speedy Hedgehog 4pc fires) 3. Swap to Main DPS immediately 4. DPS: Full skill rotation inside the ATK buff window (20s) 5. Sub-DPS: Skill + any off-field hits while ATK buff is still active 6. Adler: Skill (Evil's Bane shield + DoT) 7. Repeat from Step 1 when Sakiri's ultimate is ready again
Key: Sakiri's ultimate buff lasts 20 seconds. Your entire DPS rotation should fit inside this window. If your Charge Efficiency is low, use Speedy Hedgehog on Sakiri specifically so she gets her ultimate back faster.

Baicang ETD-4 Burst Rotation

1. Skia: Skill (enter stealth, attach Fang Thrusts — triggers ETD-4 stealth cooperative attack with Baicang) 2. Fadia: Skill (Existence — damage redirect active, HP threshold primed for ETD-4 cooperative proc) 3. Lacrimosa: Skill (Tomato form switch — triggers ETD-4 bat form cooperative attack with Baicang) 4. Baicang: Skill (accumulate Power Words: Curse, Bless, Objurgate) 5. Baicang: Ultimate (Contemplative Domain — detonate all Power Words inside domain) 6. Continue Baicang basic attacks inside the domain to regenerate Power Words for second detonation 7. Swap out as domain ends, cycle supports again
Key: The three ETD-4 cooperative attack triggers (Skia stealth, Fadia HP threshold, Lacrimosa bat switch) all fire free bonus hits alongside Baicang automatically when active. Line them up before Baicang's ultimate for maximum damage density inside his domain window.

Hotori Replay Rotation

1. Main DPS: Use Skill (Hotori records this skill) 2. Hotori: Switch in, use Present Replay to record the DPS skill again if needed 3. Hotori: Ultimate (World's Tide time-stop — replays recorded skills with Cosmos DMG amp) 4. Inside time-stop: use any additional Hotori skills for extra Cosmos hits 5. Main DPS: Resume rotation as time-stop ends 6. Repeat — aim to record the highest DMG skill available each cycle
Key: Hotori replays the last recorded skill during World's Tide. Always make sure the skill recorded is your DPS's highest-damage move, not a basic attack. Time recording deliberately by switching to Hotori immediately after the DPS uses their big skill.

Daffodill Breaker Rotation

1. Lacrimosa: Skill (apply Nightmare DoT, trigger Chaos Scorch reaction for Diabolos 24% RES shred) 2. Sakiri: Skill + Ultimate (team ATK buff active) 3. Daffodill: Basic attacks to build Phantom Step charges 4. Daffodill: Ultimate (Finale — Paranormal Ace state, Insight active on enemies) 5. Inside Finale: Parry attacks to gain extra Phantom Step charges 6. Enemy Break triggered inside Finale with Insight: Break burst fires with full RES shred + ATK buff + Chaos DMG bonus 7. Adler: Skill (shield + DoT) during downtime 8. Repeat Daffodill rotation on next Finale cooldown
Key: The Daffodill break burst is most effective when Diabolos 4pc is already active (requires Scorch reaction from Lacrimosa), Sakiri's ATK buff is running, and Insight is applied before the break happens. Stacking all three simultaneously is her damage ceiling. Practice the parry timing: mastering it significantly increases Phantom Step charges and thus Finale damage output.

Resonance / Awakening Investment Priority

Awakening (also called Resonance or A1/A2/A3) refers to the additional passive effects characters unlock as you progress through their story and bond content. These are not gacha pulls; they come from completing the character's main story quests and bond levels. Here is the priority order for each tier:

TierWhat It UnlocksPriorityNotes
A1 (First Awakening)First passive improvement — usually a stat buff, cooldown reduction, or new mechanic triggerAlways unlock firstZero's A1 is guaranteed by end of Chapter 1 main story. Most characters unlock A1 from story quests automatically.
A2 (Second Awakening)Meaningful upgrade — often introduces or amplifies the character's core mechanicUnlock as soon as bond level allowsRequires reaching a specific Bond level with the character. Gift them regularly using the Bond menu. A2 is typically where a character's DPS output jumps noticeably.
A3 (Third Awakening)Final passive — usually the most impactful upgrade, completing the kitEnd-game goal, not required for storyZero's A3 is guaranteed from the main story by end of 1.0 content. Other characters require sustained Bond investment. Worth it for your main DPS and primary support; lower priority on bench characters.
Zero Specifically: Zero's full Awakening (A1 through A3) is unlocked automatically through main story progression in version 1.0. You will have it all by the time you finish the story. For other characters, prioritize bond gifts during daily play and let it progress naturally rather than burning resources to rush it.
Investment Order: For everyone except Zero, prioritize Awakening on your main DPS (A1 and A2 first), then your primary healer or buffer (A1 at minimum), then secondary DPS. Do not spread bond gifts across all characters equally: concentrated investment is faster.

Quick Rule: If your S-rank Module rolled two of your top three stats (Crit Rate / Crit DMG / ATK% for DPS), keep it and upgrade it. If it rolled only one top-three stat or zero, treat it as a farming placeholder and keep looking. Don't lock in mediocre gear just because it's S-rank.

Stat Priority Quick Reference — By Role

Use this as a fast lookup when evaluating Module rolls. Priority 1 is always your first target; anything past Priority 4 is a bonus, not a requirement.
